Wiring design KELLY SIDE UNVERIFIED

    
    
      
  1. Limp. OUT3 (Teensy pin 20) drives a PC817 opto whose transistor pulls the KLS low-speed switch input to its RTN. Max speed in limp is set in the Kelly config tool and caps speed, not battery amps. KLS pin number: read it off Adam's harness or the KLS manual.
    2. 
      
  2. Derate. OUT5 (pin 2) PWM, duty = allowance %. Planned: RC filter to a DC level that scales the throttle wiper (CD4066 analog switch or MCP4131 digital pot). Part choice and values not picked yet.
    3. 
      
  3. Regen. OUT6 (pin 3) HIGH = regen allowed, through a PC817 in series with the KLS regen or brake-switch input. Which KLS input does regen on this controller is unverified.
    4. 
      
  4. Hard stop. Real faults still open the EV200 mains through the contactor sequence; cutback is the soft layer in front of that.
    5. 
    

    
Full notes: docs/KELLY_CUTBACK.md.

Gear

      
Vehicle model (sim/vehicle.js): motor torque = throttle × speed-mode scale × BMS power allowed × 550 A phase × ASSUMED Kt, capped by the 550 A Kelly battery limit; wheel speed from mass, Crr, CdA, grade (ASSUMED) and 24" stock tire (SOURCED: Adam), 16/32 sprockets × 4.375 diff = 8.75 (SOURCED), edit in Settings; motor RPM = wheel speed × ratio. Brake pressure = regen first up to the PROPOSED 60 A max (Kelly Brake_AN, pin 2, analog regen — pin per brief, UNVERIFIED on the harness), friction tops up; regen fades out below ~3 mph and only flows if the BMS allows regen. Speed-mode scales/RPM caps (H 100 %/6000, M 70 %/4400, L 45 %/2700, R 25 %/1100) are PROPOSED. Throttle is ignored while plugged in. Top speed falls as the pack drains (SOURCED: Sparky, back-EMF 0.026 V/RPM): base speed ≈ pack V ÷ 0.026 = ≈5680 RPM (≈46 mph) at 147.6 V full, ≈5120 RPM (≈42 mph) at 133 V nominal, ≈4570 RPM (≈37 mph) at the 118.8 V low cut; above base speed the Kelly must field-weaken, up to the 6000 RPM cap (≈49 mph). mph from the 24" tire and 8.75 ratio; sag under load lowers it further (not modelled).

Drive cycle SIM PROFILE · NOT LOGGED DATA

    

    

    

    
Plays scripted throttle, brake and gear into the driver inputs above, so pack current, cutback, regen, trips and SoC all come from the real BmsCore. Turns the key on if needed and keeps driving on any tab. Stops early if the mains open. Profiles are made up for testing, not logged Teryx drives; speed and distance come from the toy speed model (PROPOSED gear caps). Use 5× or 20× for the long climb.

  

  
State of charge SIM · NOT IN FIRMWARE

    

      

    

    
Estimate = the firmware's own BmsCore::Soc (include/SocEstimator.h) run on LEM A + LEM B, + = discharge. It is unknown at boot and only becomes known at a full-charge anchor (Core "at charge limit"); current invalid for more than 2 s makes it unknown again. capacity 180 Ah = 4 strings (SOURCED: Adam, 36S × 4P) × 45 Ah per group (ASSUMED); the real bank Ah is UNVERIFIED and is 0 = unknown in code. Sim truth = lowest cell on a SIM-ASSUMED linear map 3.30 V = 0 % → 4.10 V = 100 % (no verified OCV curve). Not wired in firmware: CURRENT_SENSE_ENABLE=0.

Settings SIM ONLY

    
These change the simulator only and are saved in this browser (localStorage). They never change firmware, the Kelly or any flag. Firmware defaults stay as committed until Adam approves a change.

    

    

    
Read-only rows come from the firmware build (BmsCore config) and can only change in code. The BMS trip, temperature, sag, imbalance and derate-log levels are editable in BMS thresholds below.

  

  
BMS thresholds SIM · SAME RULES AS FIRMWARE

    

    
The real include/Thresholds.h (serial T command) runs inside the simulator: same bounds, same tighten-only trips and temperature cuts, same order rules. Applied values go straight into the simulated BmsCore and are saved in this browser (simulated EEPROM 1216–1305). Firmware and the Teensy are not changed. Bounds are software sanity limits, not part specs.

Fault log SURVIVES POWER-OFF

    

    
—

    

    
Real include/FaultLog.h running on a simulated Teensy 4.1 EEPROM (bytes 256–1215, 48 records × 20 B, CRC-16 each). It keeps fault set/clear edges and every derate (power cutback, with its reason and lowest %) across power cycles, Reset and page reloads (saved in this browser). Limits: same edge once per second, 24 records per boot, derates capped at 12 per boot so real faults always have room. A derate is logged once it holds 100 ms and cleared after 1 s at full power (PLACEHOLDER). Firmware does not write this log yet, and real flash endurance is UNVERIFIED.
